The method is used in games that feature real-time terrain modification and require consistent frame rates [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method is used in games that 'feature real-time terrain modification'. While Source [S1] explicitly mentions 'terrain modification' (blocks being placed, dirty chunks, remeshing), Source [S2] describes a system for 'VoxelBody objects' and mentions a 'Mode switch' that marks bodies dirty, but does not explicitly describe real-time terrain modification (like player-placed blocks) as a feature of the games using this specific engine code. More importantly, the claim states the method is used in games that 'require consistent frame rates'. The evidence in [S1] explicitly states 'the frame rate with blocks is unmeasured' and suggests running a benchmark on a real machine, implying that consistent frame rates are not guaranteed or measured by this specific implementation. Source [S2] mentions preventing main-thread stalls, which helps consistency, but the combination of 'real-time terrain modification' (not clearly supported by S2's 'VoxelBody' focus) and the explicit lack of measured consistent frame rates in S1 makes the claim unsupported by the provided evidence.
supported
- **Time Complexity:** O(N) where N is the number of dirty chunks, but bounded by the time budget [S1].

The claim states that the time complexity is O(N) where N is the number of dirty chunks, but bounded by the time budget. The evidence explicitly states that 'Dirty chunks are added to a RemeshQueue ordered nearest to the camera first' and are 'meshed until 3 ms of the frame are spent, always at least one chunk.' This confirms that the processing iterates through the dirty chunks (implying a linear relationship with the number of processed chunks, hence O(N) relative to the set of dirty chunks considered) and is strictly capped by the 3 ms time budget.

It prevents main-thread stalls by limiting the number of sub-chunks remeshed per frame and capping the total time spent on geometry generation [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the system 'Manages GPU mesh generation for VoxelBody objects with a per-frame budget to prevent main-thread stalls.' It further specifies that it 'remeshes only dirty sub-chunks, respecting time and count limits,' and defines constants `MaxRebuildsPerFrame` (limiting the number of sub-chunks) and `RebuildBudgetMs` (limiting the total time). This directly supports the claim that it prevents main-thread stalls by limiting sub-chunks remeshed per frame and capping geometry generation time.
